verified.item: Discount factor applied to the terminal value
verified.report_says: "The terminal value is capitalised at the terminal rate and brought home on year five's own cumulative factor — one date, one price of time." Table 7 prints that factor as 0.4521 (and Table 9 applies 0.4521 to FY2030 free cash flow).
verified.actually_correct: The model does not use 0.4521. Workbook DCF!B29 is 1/((1+r26)^0.5 x (1+r27)(1+r28)(1+r29)(1+r30)) = 1/(1.276^0.5 x 1.2409 x 1.2129 x 1.1960 x 1.1834) = 1/2.40626 = 0.41558, and the cell's own label reads "End-of-window discount factor (t = 4.417y, not the year-5 mid-point)". My rebuild: terminal free cash flow 3,310.1, TV = 3,310.1 x 1.07 / (0.18342 - 0.07) = 31,227; 31,227 x 0.41558 = 12,977, which is the printed PV of terminal value of 12,976. At the factor the study says it uses: 31,227 x 0.4521 = 14,118.
verified.why_it_failed: The document asserts one construction and the delivered workbook performs a different one, and the workbook's own cell comment states the difference explicitly. Half of the enterprise value (53.5%) is discounted on a factor that appears nowhere in the study. Either the sentence is false or the model is; they cannot both stand.
verified.impact: +EGP 1,142mn of enterprise value, +EGP 3.05/share, +4.6% on the EGP 66.53 headline (66.53 -> 69.58) if the printed claim were followed. The end-of-window factor is arguably the better construction; what fails is the printed description of it.

verified.location: §1.8, "The terminal block is therefore struck on REPLACEMENT-COST invested capital — EGP 51,191mn, being 5.0Mt at USD 130 a tonne"
verified.report_says: EGP 51,191mn = 5.0Mt at USD 130 per annual tonne.
verified.actually_correct: 5.0 x 130 = USD 650mn. At the model's own valuation-date rate (Assumptions!B11 = USD/EGP 50.30, the rate the asset lens uses: 5.0 x 95 x 50.30 + 687 = 24,580, /374.867 = 65.57, the published asset-lens value) that is EGP 32,695mn. The printed 51,191 requires a further undisclosed multiplication by the cumulative local cost-inflation index to FY2030 (Assumptions!G29 = 1.565711): 5.0 x 130 x 50.30 x 1.565711 = 51,190.9. Workbook DCF!A22 says so — "in TERMINAL-year pounds" — the study does not.
verified.why_it_failed: A stated total does not reproduce from its two stated operands; it is 56.6% larger. The same USD 130/t is worth EGP 32,695mn in the asset lens and EGP 51,191mn in the terminal block of the same model, with nothing on the page reconciling them. A reader checking the single most consequential judgement in the model cannot arrive at the number.
verified.impact: The charge it drives is maintenance = 51,191/20 = EGP 2,560mn a year. On the printed operands it would be 32,695/20 = 1,635mn: terminal FCF 4,235 instead of 3,310, TV 39,952, FV EGP 76.20 — +14.5% on the headline. The escalation is defensible; the description is not.

A figure of 11.3% appears in the earlier editions of this section and is NOT used here: it divides a profit already grown by one year of terminal growth by a capital base that has not grown." verified.location: Study §1.4 Table 6 ("The two anchors"), beta row: 0.928 explicit / 1.074 terminal; and §1.5, the full page on the beta
verified.item: The terminal cost of equity uses a beta 15.8% higher than the one the study explains, and neither the construction nor its tax rate appears in the document a reader receives
verified.report_says: Table 6 prints "Beta 0.928 / 1.074" with no note. Its caption explains only the default-spread netting. §1.5 is titled "Beta, and why it is a peer estimate rather than a regression", runs a full page, adopts 0.928 as the peer median of 0.815/0.919/0.936/1.030, prices the alternative at +12.0%, and publishes a whole sensitivity table across 0.60-1.30 — and never once mentions that a second, different beta governs the terminal. The bibliography's judgements table is the same: "Beta — 0.928 adopted", no terminal beta. The words relever, unlever, Hamada and target structure appear nowhere in either document, and no tax rate for the relevering is stated in any of the three delivered artefacts.
verified.actually_correct: I recovered the construction by arithmetic before finding any label for it. Unlever the adopted beta at the observed structure and relever at the terminal weight, at Egypt's statutory rate: D/E_obs = 0.037841/0.962159 = 0.039329; βU = 0.9275220650537075/(1 + 0.775 x 0.039329) = 0.900090; D/E_term = 0.20/0.80 = 0.25; βL = 0.900090 x (1 + 0.775 x 0.25) = 1.074483 — the printed figure to six decimals, and the implied tax rate solves to exactly 22.50%, Egypt's statutory rate, which Damodaran's January-2026 file independently confirms. The delivered WORKBOOK does name it, once, in a label cell: DCF!E47 "Terminal beta, UNLEVERED at the observed structure then re-levered", formula C47 referencing Assumptions!$B$8 "Statutory tax rate" 0.225. So the construction is named in one delivered artefact and in no other, and the tax rate is stated in none — it is recoverable only by following a cell reference. Note also that the same model carries two tax rates without reconciling them anywhere: the relevering and both after-tax costs of debt use the statutory 22.5%, while every NOPAT line uses the effective 23.82%.
verified.why_it_failed: The house test is that a terminal beta different from the explicit one must NAME its construction and STATE its tax rate. The study document does neither, and it is the study document that carries the beta section, the beta sensitivity and the beta judgement. A reader of the delivered study cannot tell 1.074 from a typing error, and a reader of §1.5 is actively told that the beta in this valuation is 0.928.
verified.impact: About -4.2% of enterprise value, i.e. the relevering is worth that much of the headline. Carrying the same beta into the terminal gives Ke = 12.50% + 0.9275 x 7.00% = 18.993% and a terminal WACC of 17.519% against the published 18.342%; on the study's own terminal growth of 7.00% the capitalisation spread widens from 11.342 to 10.519, lifting terminal value 7.8%, and terminal value is 53.5% of enterprise value per the study's own Table 10. The relevering is a legitimate construction and I am not saying the number is wrong — the >3% sits on an undisclosed choice.

verified.location: Study §1.4 Table 6, "Equity risk premium 9.41%"; bibliography input register #175 (erp_cds) and #182 (sov_spread_cds)
verified.item: Damodaran's January-2026 file publishes two premium bases for Egypt and the study adopts the cheaper one without disclosing, naming or pricing the other
verified.report_says: #175 "erp_cds 0.0941 Country Egypt equity risk premium, CDS-based, Damodaran January-2026" and #182 "sov_spread_cds 0.034 ... Damodaran January-2026 country risk file, CDS column". Table 6 prints one premium. Neither the study nor the bibliography anywhere mentions that the same file also publishes a rating-based basis, names the adopted basis as central against an alternative, or prices the difference.
verified.actually_correct: The cited file (pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/New_Home_Page/datafile/ctryprem.html, update dated 5 January 2026) carries both bases for Egypt on the same row: rating Caa1, adjusted default spread 6.37%, country risk premium 9.71%, total equity risk premium 13.94% — alongside sovereign CDS 3.41% and CDS-based ERP 9.41%. Recomputing the study's own construction on the rating basis, with country risk still counted exactly once and consistently: rf* = 22.95% - 6.37% = 16.58%; Ke = 16.58% + 0.9275220650537075 x 13.94% = 29.510%; explicit WACC = 0.96216 x 29.510% + 0.03784 x 10.3524% = 28.785%, against the published 27.600% — 118.5 basis points higher. (Separately, the file gives the CDS spread as 3.41% and the study carries 3.40%; that 1bp is rounding and is not the finding.)
verified.why_it_failed: Both bases are published by the source the study cites, they differ by 453bp of premium, and the one adopted is the one that produces the lower discount rate and the higher value. A reader is shown neither the alternative nor the fact that a choice was made.
verified.impact: About -1.4% of enterprise value on the explicit window alone: 118.5bp over an average discounting period of roughly 2.5 years across FY2026E-FY2030E, applied to the 46.5% of enterprise value that sits outside the terminal. Materially larger if the same basis were carried into the terminal premium, which the study does not address.

verified.location: Study §1.10, Table 14 "Discount rate" row and the paragraph beneath it, against Table 7 in the same document
verified.item: The study publishes two mutually irreconcilable accounts of its own discount-rate schedule, and states the same reconciliation bar twice at values 6.35 EGP/share apart
verified.report_says: Table 14 row: "Discount rate | -6.19 | their flat 20.06% vs our 24.5%→14.5%". The paragraph: "Discount rate (-6.19, open — no referee) ... their year-5 factor of 0.4813 is harsher than our 0.4876. The two errors very nearly cancel and the whole bar is EGP 0.16, so neither convention is worth arguing over." Table 7, eleven pages earlier, publishes the schedule as 27.60% / 24.09% / 21.29% / 19.60% / 18.34% with a FY2030E cumulative discount factor of 0.4521, and §7 quotes "a hurdle of 18.34%".
verified.actually_correct: Only Table 7 reproduces. Its five discount factors follow exactly from 27.60%→18.34% on the printed glide fractions and the model's stub-and-mid-period convention (0.9409, 0.7947, 0.6478, 0.5378, 0.4521), and 18.34% reproduces from the printed terminal inputs. Neither "24.5%→14.5%" nor "0.4876" reproduces from anything either document publishes: I rebuilt the factor path under the 24.5→14.5 endpoints on the same glide fractions and got 0.5076 mid-period and 0.4550 end-of-period, and neither is 0.4876. The comparison the sentence draws also inverts on the study's own figures: EFG's 1/1.2006^4 = 0.4813 is confirmed, and against Table 7's published 0.4521 it is the study's own factor that is harsher, not EFG's. And "the whole bar is EGP 0.16" contradicts the -6.19 printed in the row above it and used consistently elsewhere in the same section (+9.77 - 6.19 = +3.58, which the text states).
verified.why_it_failed: The section is presented as a bar-by-bar reconciliation whose "bars sum to the gap exactly", i.e. as something a reader can check. On the discount-rate bar a reader cannot: the schedule quoted is not the schedule the model runs, the year-five factor quoted is not the one Table 7 publishes, the direction of the comparison reverses on the published figures, and the bar's value is stated twice 38 times apart.
verified.impact: None on the published central of EGP 66.53 — the bridge's endpoint is the published central and Table 7 is what the model runs. The damage is to verifiability: 6.35 EGP/share of stated disagreement, 9.5% of the central, sits inside one paragraph.

verified.why_it_failed: The delivered source register cites a figure (5% Q4-2028) that does not build the delivered rate, and the construction that does build it is the one the study's own caveats section says was a defect and has been corrected. The perpetuity therefore assumes Egypt never reaches its own published 2028 inflation target, for ever.
verified.impact: Understates fair value. On the source the bibliography cites, the terminal risk-free rate falls 200bp to 10.50%, terminal cost of equity to 18.02% and terminal WACC to 16.74%. Read off the study's OWN published Table 12 (EGP 66.53 at an 18.3% terminal rate, 71.06 at 17.3%, 76.55 at 16.3%), that puts fair value near EGP 75, roughly +12%. The growth leg barely offsets: the study's own Table 11 moves only EGP 4.43 across the entire 3-7% row.

verified.location: Workbook Assumptions!B143 (0.8711327) and B144 (0.9763642), applied in Segments rows 57 and 65-67; narrated in study section 1.6 and Table 3
verified.item: Two undisclosed multiplicative level-shift calibrations, applied to every forecast year, are what make the margin rise; the declared price and cost paths on their own make it fall
verified.report_says: Section 1.6: "Local prices are assumed to grow 51.7% in total across the five years while pound costs grow 56.6% — a real erosion of about 3%." Segments row 56 multiplies the local price by Assumptions!B142 = 1.078760 (+7.88%, disclosed); rows 65-67 multiply EVERY cost line by B144 = 0.976364 (-2.36%, NOT disclosed in the study or in the 212-entry bibliography); row 57 multiplies the export price by B143 = 0.871133 (-12.89%, NOT disclosed in either document). The relative price-vs-cost shift is 1.078760/0.976364 = +10.49%, four times the declared five-year real wedge of -3.14%. The -3.14% the study prints is 1.516563/1.565711 - 1, i.e. price index against COST INDEX — the comparison the same paragraph says has been superseded. verified.why_it_failed: The sentence performs the correction it announces and then quotes the uncorrected number as the result of it. verified.impact: No direct effect on the arithmetic (the model already runs on the calibrated numbers), but it misstates the direction of the single judgement the study calls central. verified.location: Workbook Assumptions!B28 (USD/EGP path), FY2026 cell = 55.11; against B11 = 50.3; bibliography entry 178 and the country ring, "currency", 2026-08-04
verified.item: The FY2026 exchange rate that anchors the entire currency path is hand-set 9.6% above the study's own observed spot, and the delivered study never prints it
verified.report_says: Bibliography entry 178: "USD/EGP path: FY2025 actual average, then the house currency path — relative purchasing-power parity on the house inflation path against long-run foreign inflation, DERIVED and never hand-set. The retired path was typed... and depreciated the pound at roughly two-thirds of the inflation differential the same model applied to costs, which is one event counted once and ignored once." The research trail's country/currency ring: "The pound has been broadly stable around EGP 50.3-51.0 per US dollar through July and early August 2026." The delivered study prints no exchange rate at all.
verified.actually_correct: I tested the PPP claim on the path itself. FY2027-FY2030 reproduce relative PPP against 2.50% foreign inflation to two decimals: (1.12/1.025)-1 = 9.27% vs the path's 9.27%; (1.09/1.025)-1 = 6.34% vs 6.34%; (1.075/1.025)-1 = 4.88% vs 4.89%; (1.07/1.025)-1 = 4.39% vs 4.38%. FY2026 does NOT: 55.11/49.26 = +11.88%, which backs out a foreign inflation of MINUS 0.34%. PPP on the house path off the FY2025 average gives 49.26 x 1.0878 = 53.59; off the observed valuation-date spot it gives about 50-51. 55.11 reproduces from nothing stated. It also requires the pound to average 55.11 across calendar 2026 having started the year at the audited 47.66 year-end (bibliography entry 80) and been "broadly stable" at 50.3-51.0 in July/August — i.e. roughly EGP 67/USD from September to December, a devaluation of a third in four months that appears in no document.
verified.why_it_failed: The one step of the currency path that is NOT derived is the level, and every later year is PPP off it, so the hand-set anchor propagates through the whole window. It is the exact failure the bibliography names in the path it retired.
verified.impact: Material and value-inflating. Re-anchoring FY2026 to the observed spot (50.0/50.3/51.0) and running the model's own PPP rates forward gives EGP 62.67 / 62.89 / 63.42 — a fall of 4.7% to 5.8% from EGP 66.53. Honest caveat: the export leg carries the undisclosed 0.8711 calibration struck on the reviewed H1-2026 half, which may already absorb part of the FX overstatement; the capex leg carries no calibration and is unambiguously 9.6% too high in every year (worth +1.0% on its own).

verified.report_says: 'More useful for a forecast is the exit rate: the fourth quarter of 2025 realised EGP 3,118 a tonne, 7.2% ABOVE the full-year average. Holding that exit flat through 2026 would by itself produce a full-year average 7.2% higher, so the 8.0% carried here is less than a point above a path in which prices stop rising altogether. verified.actually_correct: Segments!C56 = base local price x Assumptions!C26 x Assumptions!B142, i.e. two multipliers, not one. Base local price = 8,350.45461 / 2.92332Mt = EGP 2,856.5/t. FY2026E local price = 2,856.5 x 1.08 x 1.078760 = EGP 3,327.9/t, which is +16.50% on FY2025, not +8.0%. COULD NOT READ: the three audited PDFs (ARCC_FY2023/FY2024/FY2025_Consolidated_Financials.pdf) and the Q1-2026 interim are image-only scans — pdftotext returns 47 bytes — so the audited line items themselves are UNVERIFIABLE from here and I tested them only for internal consistency against the presentation and against each other. NOT READ, per instruction: study_numbers.json, diagnostics.json, compute.py, the GAP_REVIEW files, anything under /scripts/. No public copy of the EFG Hermes 6-Aug-2026 note was found, so all of section 1.10's counterparty figures are unverifiable.

verified.location: §1.4 Table 7 caption; §1.7 Table 10 (PV of terminal value 12,976)
verified.item: The terminal value is not discounted on the factor the page prints
verified.report_says: Table 7 prints the FY2030 cumulative discount factor as 0.4521, and its caption states: 'The terminal value is capitalised at the terminal rate and brought home on year five's own cumulative factor — one date, one price of time.'
verified.actually_correct: The delivered workbook uses a DIFFERENT, unprinted factor. DCF!B29 is labelled 'End-of-window discount factor (t = 4.417y, not the year-5 mid-point)' = 1/((1.2760)^0.5 x 1.2409 x 1.2129 x 1.1960 x 1.1834) = 0.41558, against Table 7's mid-year 0.4521 = 1/((1.2760)^0.5 x 1.2409 x 1.2129 x 1.1960 x (1.1834)^0.5). Back out the terminal value from the printed PV: 12,976 / 0.41558 = EGP 31,225mn. Apply the factor the caption says is used: 31,225 x 0.4521 = EGP 14,117mn. EV = 11,277 + 14,117 = 25,394; equity = 25,394 + 687 = 26,081; 26,081 / 374.867 = EGP 69.58.
verified.why_it_failed: The caption asserts one date and one price of time; the model in fact discounts the explicit flows to their mid-years and the terminal value to the end of the window. That may well be the better convention, but a reader following the printed instruction cannot reproduce the published answer and is told, wrongly, that they can.
verified.impact: +4.6% on the headline (EGP 69.58 against the published EGP 66.53) if the printed instruction is followed literally.

verified.location: Overview p.3; §1.8; Appendix B.2; B.3 first bullet
verified.item: The 96% sector-utilisation claim mixes clinker into a cement-only denominator — the exact error the study says it corrected
verified.report_says: 'Egypt sold about 72.6 million tonnes against roughly 76 million tonnes of nameplate — a market running near 96%, which is NOT the structurally slack market earlier editions of this study described.' B.2 calls this 'the correction [that] matters beyond tidiness'.
verified.actually_correct: ARCC's own FY2025 Investor Presentation (p.12 Egyptian Cement Market Overview, FY2025 column) gives Cement Domestic Sales 53,992.9 kt, Cement Export Sales 11,063.0 kt and Clinker Export Sales 7,568.9 kt. Cement-only national sales = 53,992.9 + 11,063.0 = 65,055.9 kt = 65.06Mt. Against a 76Mt CEMENT nameplate that is 65.06/76 = 85.6%, not 96%. The 72.6Mt numerator adds 7.57Mt of exported CLINKER to cement sales. Global Cement, 'Update on Egypt, October 2025', which is the source the study cites for the 76Mt: '76Mt/yr from 46 production lines… Domestic consumption was estimated at 46Mt/yr and exports at 20Mt/yr giving a utilisation rate 87%'. EnterpriseAM: Egyptian production Jan-Sep 2025 was 47.8Mt, ~64Mt annualised.
verified.why_it_failed: The study's own bibliography (entry 59) says the earlier balance failed because 'it set a cement-plus-clinker export figure against a cement-only production figure'. The replacement does precisely that, in the other direction, and the earlier 65Mt figure it discards was in fact correct and closed exactly (65.06 − 53.99 = 11.06 = cement exports). This is the premise on which the edition raised the local price path from ~3-4%/yr to 8.0/9.0/8.0/7.0/6.5% and called the market tight rather than slack.
verified.impact: Directionally overstates value. The margin sensitivity printed at Table 22 is EGP 2.46 a share per point of EBITDA margin, and the price path is the largest driver of that margin; the tight-market premise supports the whole 39.0%→40.4% path.

verified.location: §1.2, paragraph beginning 'The reconstruction reproduces audited FY2025 revenue to +0.000%'
verified.item: A validation presented as a test that could fail is an algebraic identity — and the delivered workbook says so
verified.report_says: 'The reconstruction reproduces audited FY2025 revenue to +0.000% and audited FY2025 EBITDA to +0.000%. It is not forced to: the volume is derived from the revenue note and the cost lines are the printed ones, so a wrong price assumption would show up as a non-zero residual.'
verified.actually_correct: Segments!B22 sets local price = local revenue / local volume; Segments!B59 then rebuilds local revenue = local volume x that price. Substituting, reconstructed local revenue = local volume x (local revenue / local volume) = local revenue, for ANY volume. The export leg is the same identity through the cement-equivalent tonnage (B25→B26→B57/B58→B60+B61), and services are goods x (services/goods). The delivered workbook states it in terms: Segments rows 83-84, 'Rows 76-81 are a TIE, not a test: with prices derived from revenue, revenue reconstructs by construction. Revision 3 presented exactly this identity as "a test that can fail". It cannot.'
verified.why_it_failed: The document presents to the reader, as independent corroboration, the very identity its own workbook flags as incapable of failing — and which §1.2 elsewhere condemns as the structural failure of three earlier editions.
verified.impact: No effect on the arithmetic; removes the only validation the reader is offered for the FY2025 unit build.
